title: Transactional change participants and the Audit journal on them
summary: Write operations hand their committed-attempt records to `ChangeParticipant`s inside the operation transaction through the append-only `OwnedRowsWriter` (`Changes\Internal\OperationRows`), with `ChangeRecord` carrying the core-built event; the public `ChangeJournal` sink and `DatabaseSource::appendJournal()` are gone; the audit journal is `Audit\Internal\JournalParticipant` + `Audit\Internal\JournalRow`; `Storage\Schema\IdentityColumns` and the participant contract suite exist; `ContractWorld::rowCounts()` counts only the current schema.
why: D8/R6: the journal needs exactly same-transaction append of rows carrying the published event ids; an append-only capability limited to declared tables is the narrowest contract, and core must stop hard-coding the audit table (I2, I13 entries). Hard risks (participant-model): rows of discarded attempts must vanish on rollback, nested host rollback and deadlock retry; events are built once and dispatched only after the root commit; a participant can never touch authority tables.

include: New `Contracts\Changes\ChangeParticipant`, `Contracts\Changes\OwnedRowsWriter`, `Changes\ChangeRecord` exactly as knowledge/contracts#participants; `PanelBuilder::participants()` (contracts#panel-builder); compile checks of p2-execution#participant-model

`ChangePipeline::operate()`: events built once per change result; after the last change, if any effect, participants called in declaration order with records in effect order and a new `Changes\Internal\OperationRows` bound to the active `StorageMutation`; the window closes when `record()` returns

Retire the public `Changes\ChangeJournal` (row encoding → `Audit\Internal\JournalRow`, 14 columns, payload JSON of `AccessEvent::toArray()`); `Plugins\Audit\RecordChange` → `Audit\Internal\JournalParticipant` (`tables(): ['audit_log']`); `AuditPlugin::register()` contributes `participants([JournalParticipant::class])` instead of the pipe; `DatabaseSource::appendJournal()` removed; files under packages/core/src/Audit/Internal (D17)
New `Storage\Schema\IdentityColumns` (Spi(Call), contracts#storage) built on `HostKeyColumns`; core `StorageSchema` may use it only if DDL snapshots stay byte-identical (I15)
New `Testing\Contracts\ChangeParticipantContractTests` (Spi(Call)): window, declared tables, scalar values, rollback, retry re-invocation, no call on no-op
Fix `Testing\Contracts\ContractWorld::rowCounts()` to list tables of the current database/schema only (P1 note; MySQL vacuity) and add a test that fails on the old behavior

Re-target I11/I6/I12 suites: tests/Feature/Plugins/Audit, TransactionPropertiesTest, NestedMutationTest, ChangeRaceTest, TransactionTest, DirectWritesEngineTest; events snapshot and audit-rows snapshot unchanged
Inactive-cost allowlist: `ChangeJournal` module-service entry removed; i2 ChangeJournal entries removed; `pruneJournal` stays (P3)
Migration lines: ChangeJournal → ChangeParticipant + OwnedRowsWriter; journaling pipes → participants
exclude: Audit schema/migration/adoption, prune without panel lock, health split (P3)

reads.why: Rules every P2 item follows (reference wins, no shims, D17 placement, attributes, snapshots, migration lines)
Report-mode allowlist protocol and which entries this item removes
Exact validation commands and driver environment
Owners/roots, Internal placement rule, stable FQCNs, composition roots — where new files go
Transaction invariant, enforcement points, bypass routes and interfering pairs
Chain G and its case table
audit_log format that must not change
Row encoding to move, frame sink to retire

rules: One journal row per effective change with the dispatched event's eventId; none for no-op, rollback, nested rollback, discarded retry (I11) — asserted on all drivers.
Formats/audit-rows.json and Formats/events.json pass without regeneration (row and payload shape unchanged).
`OperationRows` never exposes a builder, connection or the mutation; capability misuse raises UnsupportedDirectWriteException (I6).
